problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\frac{1}{x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}({x}^{3})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(4x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & =\frac{1}{x} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})=\frac{2}{{x}^{3}} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})=-\frac{6}{{x}^{4}} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
A={\frac{1}{x},-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},\frac{2}{{x}^{3}},-\frac{6}{{x}^{4}},…}
$$

Consequently, $A$ is infinite.

- The set $B$ is finite. Listing a few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & ={x}^{3} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})=3{x}^{2} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2})=6x \\ {g}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x)=6 \\ {g}^{(4)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6)=0 \\ {g}^{(5)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(0)=0 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, for $n>4,$ we have ${g}^{(n)}(x)=0.$ Listing a few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
B={{x}^{3},3{x}^{2},6x,6,0}.
$$

Consequently, $|B|=5,$ which is finite.

- The set $C$ is also finite. Listing a few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & =4x \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)=4 \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4)=0 \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(0)=0 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, for $n>2,$ we have ${h}^{(n)}(x)=0.$ Listing a few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
C={4x,4,0}.
$$

Consequently, $|C|=3,$ which is finite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only."
